text: Green means no warning: no significant severe weather is expected, so no specific action is needed beyond normal precautions.
Yellow means watch and stay updated: be aware of developing weather conditions and keep checking for the latest forecasts, as the situation could worsen.
Orange means be prepared: severe weather is likely, so people should stay alert, prepare for disruption, and follow guidance from local authorities.
Red means take action: very severe weather is expected, so people should follow official advisories, avoid unnecessary travel, and take protective action immediately.
Light rain is classified as rainfall of less than 15.6 millimetres in a day.
Moderate rain is classified as rainfall between 15.6 and 64.4 millimetres in a day.
Heavy rain is classified as rainfall between 64.5 and 115.5 millimetres in a day.
Very heavy rain is classified as rainfall between 115.6 and 204.4 millimetres in a day.
Extremely heavy rain is classified as rainfall of 204.5 millimetres or more in a day.

A heat wave is declared when the maximum temperature reaches at least 40°C in the plains (or 30°C in hilly areas) and departs from the normal by 4.5°C or more, or when the actual maximum temperature reaches 45°C or more regardless of departure from normal.
A severe heat wave is declared when the departure from normal maximum temperature is 6.5°C or more, or when the actual maximum temperature reaches 47°C or more.
A cold wave is declared when the minimum temperature drops to 10°C or below and departs from normal by 4.5°C or more, or when the minimum temperature falls to 4°C or below.
Calm winds are those below about 1 km/h, with smoke rising vertically and no noticeable air movement felt.
Light wind (roughly 6-19 km/h) is enough to rustle leaves and be felt on the face, but causes no difficulty for normal outdoor activity.
Moderate wind (roughly 20-38 km/h) raises dust and loose paper and moves small branches; small boats and light fishing gear should be handled with care.
Strong wind (roughly 39-61 km/h) sways large branches and makes walking against it difficult; fishers are advised not to venture into the sea under these conditions.
Gale-force wind (roughly 62 km/h and above) can break branches and damage structures; all boats should stay in harbour and outdoor activity should be avoided.
A UV index of 0-2 is Low: no protection is generally needed, though sunglasses help on bright days.
A UV index of 3-5 is Moderate: seek shade during midday hours and wear sunscreen, a hat and sunglasses.
A UV index of 6-7 is High: reduce time in the sun between 10am and 4pm and use sunscreen, protective clothing, a hat and sunglasses.
A UV index of 8-10 is Very High: minimise sun exposure during midday hours and take full precautions — sunscreen, protective clothing, a hat and sunglasses.
A UV index of 11 or above is Extreme: avoid sun exposure between 10am and 4pm and take all precautions, as unprotected skin and eyes can be damaged in minutes.
"Isolated" rainfall means less than 25% of the forecast area is expected to receive rain.
"Scattered" rainfall means 25-50% of the forecast area is expected to receive rain.
"Fairly widespread" rainfall means 51-75% of the forecast area is expected to receive rain.
"Widespread" rainfall means more than 75% of the forecast area is expected to receive rain.

"Chance of rain" is a forecast probability for a future period, while "rain so far" is the amount already measured and accumulated since a fixed start time, such as midnight — the two are not interchangeable.
